brief: GS's Sentiment Indicator has fallen to -0.9, matching March's low. Market breadth has narrowed to its weakest since the Dot-Com Bubble: the S&P 500 is 1% below its record high, the median stock 16% below its own 52-week high. GS reads this as room for broad upside and a catch-up by laggards if macro uncertainty eases. The S&P 500 is up 14% YTD in total return (13% price) while consensus forward EPS rose 29%, so the forward P/E has fallen 13% this year, from 23x a year ago to 19x, matching its 10-year average. GS attributes the decline to rising real rates (real 10-year Treasury yield up 53bp in the past month, past a 2-standard-deviation threshold tied to negative equity returns) and to hyperscaler capex ($800bn this year, half of S&P 500 earnings growth) causing earnings to over-earn versus sustainable profits. Free cash flow yield (3.3%) is closer to historical norms. GS's macro model puts today's 19x P/E about 10% below fair value given rates and inflation, consistent with an ROE near 22% versus the current 24%, which GS calls justified skepticism, not pessimism. GS targets the S&P 500 at 8000 by YE2026 (4%) and 8700 in 12 months (13%).
